verses.text: In the meantime, when there were gathered together an innumerable (too many to count) multitude (crowd) of people, so that they trod one upon another, Jesus began to say to His disciples first of all: Beware of the leaven (yeast) of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy (pretending).
For there is nothing covered, that will not be revealed (shown), neither hidden, that will not be known.
Therefore whatever you have spoken in darkness will be heard in the light. And that which you have spoken in the ear in closets (inner rooms) will be proclaimed upon the housetops.
And I say to you My friends: Be not afraid of them who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
But I will forewarn (warn ahead of time) you whom you should fear: Fear Him, who after He has killed has power to cast into hell. Yes, I say to you, fear Him.
Are not 5 sparrows sold for 2 farthings (smallest coins), and not one of them is forgotten before God?
But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered (counted). Fear not therefore. You are of more value than many sparrows.
Also I say to you: Whoever will confess (say openly that they belong to) Me before men, them will the Son of man also confess before the angels of God.
But the one who denies (says they do not know) Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.
And whoever will speak a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven them. But to the one who blasphemes (speaks against) the Holy Spirit it will not be forgiven.
And when they bring you to the synagogues (meeting houses), and to magistrates (judges), and powers (rulers), take no thought (do not worry) how or what thing you will answer, or what you will say.
For the Holy Spirit will teach you in the same hour what you ought to say.
And one of the company said to Jesus: Master (Teacher), speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance (family money and land) with me.
And Jesus said to him: Man, who made Me a judge or a divider over you?

And Jesus said to them: Take heed (be careful), and beware of covetousness (wanting what belongs to others). For a person's life does not consist in the abundance (large amount) of the things which they possess.
And Jesus spoke a parable (story that teaches a lesson) to them, saying: The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully (very much).
And he thought within himself, saying: What will I do, because I have no room where to bestow (store) my fruits?
And he said: This I will do. I will pull down my barns, and build greater. And there I will bestow (store) all my fruits and my goods.
And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease (rest), eat, drink, and be merry (happy).
But God said to him: You fool, this night your soul will be required of you. Then whose will those things be, which you have provided?
So is the one who lays up treasure for themselves, and is not rich toward God.
And Jesus said to His disciples: Therefore I say to you, take no thought (do not worry) for your life, what you will eat, neither for the body, what you will put on.
The life is more than meat (food), and the body is more than raiment (clothes).
Consider the ravens. For they neither sow (plant) nor reap (harvest). They have neither storehouse nor barn, and God feeds them. How much better are you than the fowls (birds)?
And which of you by taking thought (worrying) can add to their stature (height) one cubit (about 18 inches)?
If you then are not able to do that thing which is least, why take thought (worry) for the rest?
Consider the lilies how they grow. They toil (work) not, they spin (make thread) not. And yet I say to you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed (dressed) like one of these.
If then God so clothes the grass, which is today in the field, and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith?
And do not seek what you will eat, or what you will drink, neither be of doubtful (worried) mind.
For all these things the nations of the world seek after. And your Father knows that you have need of these things.
But rather seek the kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you.
Fear not, little flock. For it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

Sell what you have, and give alms (gifts to the poor). Provide yourselves bags which do not wax (grow) old, a treasure in the heavens that does not fail, where no thief approaches (comes near), neither moth corrupts (eats up).
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Let your loins (waist) be girded about (belted, ready to work), and your lights burning,
And you yourselves like men who wait for their lord (master), when he will return from the wedding, that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him immediately.

Blessed (happy) are those servants, whom the lord (master) when he comes will find watching. Verily (truly) I say to you, that he will gird (dress) himself, and make them sit down to meat (a meal), and will come forth and serve them.
And if he will come in the second watch (time of night), or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed (happy) are those servants.
And know this, that if the goodman (owner) of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered (allowed) his house to be broken through.
Be therefore ready also, for the Son of man comes at an hour when you do not think.
Then Peter said to Jesus: Lord, do You speak this parable (story that teaches a lesson) to us, or even to all?

And the Lord said: Who then is that faithful and wise steward (manager), whom his lord (master) will make ruler over his household (family), to give them their portion of meat (food) in due season (at the right time)?
Blessed (happy) is that servant, whom his lord (master) when he comes will find so doing.
Of a truth I say to you, that he will make him ruler over all that he has.
But if that servant says in his heart: My lord (master) delays his coming, and begins to beat the menservants and maidens (servant girls), and to eat and drink, and to be drunk,

The lord (master) of that servant will come in a day when he does not look for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder (pieces), and will appoint (give) him his portion (place) with the unbelievers.
And that servant, who knew his lord's (master's) will, and did not prepare himself, neither did according to his will, will be beaten with many stripes (lashes).

But the one who did not know, and did commit things worthy of stripes (lashes), will be beaten with few stripes. For to whomever much is given, of them will much be required. And to whom men have committed (trusted) much, of them they will ask the more.
I have come to send fire on the earth. And what will I, if it is already kindled (lit)?
But I have a baptism to be baptized with. And how am I straitened (pressed hard) till it is accomplished (finished).
Do you suppose (think) that I have come to give peace on earth? I tell you: No, but rather division.
For from now on there will be 5 in one house divided, 3 against 2, and 2 against 3.

The father will be divided against the son, and the son against the father, the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother, the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.
And Jesus said also to the people: When you see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway (right away) you say: There comes a shower. And so it is.
And when you see the south wind blow, you say: There will be heat. And it comes to pass (happens).
You hypocrites (pretenders), you can discern (read) the face of the sky and of the earth. But how is it that you do not discern (understand) this time?
Yes, and why even of yourselves do you not judge what is right?

When you go with your adversary (the one taking you to court) to the magistrate (judge), as you are in the way, give diligence (work hard) that you may be delivered (set free) from him, so that he does not hale (drag) you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer cast you into prison.
I tell you, you will not depart from there, till you have paid the very last mite (smallest coin).

verses.text: There were present at that season (time) some who told Jesus of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled (mixed) with their sacrifices.
And Jesus answering said to them: Do you suppose (think) that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things?
I tell you: No. But, except you repent (change your hearts), you will all likewise perish (die).
Or those 18, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew (killed) them, do you think that they were sinners above all men who dwelt (lived) in Jerusalem?
I tell you: No. But, except you repent (change your hearts), you will all likewise perish (die).
Jesus spoke also this parable (story that teaches a lesson): A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard (grape farm). And he came and sought (looked for) fruit on it, and found none.
Then he said to the dresser (keeper) of his vineyard: Look, these 3 years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none. Cut it down. Why does it cumber (waste) the ground?
And the dresser answering said to him: Lord (sir), let it alone this year also, till I dig about it, and dung (fertilize) it.
And if it bears fruit, well. And if not, then after that you will cut it down.
And Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues (meeting houses) on the sabbath (day of rest).
And look, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity (sickness) 18 years, and was bowed together (bent over), and could in no way lift up herself.
And when Jesus saw her, He called her to Him, and said to her: Woman, you are loosed (set free) from your infirmity (sickness).
And Jesus laid His hands on her. And immediately she was made straight, and glorified (praised) God.

And the ruler of the synagogue (meeting house) answered with indignation (anger), because Jesus had healed on the sabbath day (day of rest), and said to the people: There are 6 days in which men ought to work. In them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.

The Lord then answered him, and said: You hypocrite (pretender), does not each one of you on the sabbath (day of rest) loose (untie) his ox or his ass (donkey) from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound, look, these 18 years, be loosed (set free) from this bond on the sabbath day (day of rest)?
And when Jesus had said these things, all His adversaries (enemies) were ashamed. And all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by Him.
Then Jesus said: What is the kingdom of God like? And to what will I resemble (compare) it?

It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden. And it grew, and waxed (grew into) a great tree. And the fowls (birds) of the air lodged (rested) in the branches of it.
And again Jesus said: To what will I liken (compare) the kingdom of God?
It is like leaven (yeast), which a woman took and hid in 3 measures of meal (flour), till the whole was leavened (raised by the yeast).
And Jesus went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.
Then one said to Jesus: Lord, are there few who are saved? And He said to them:
Strive (work hard) to enter in at the strait (narrow) gate. For many, I say to you, will seek to enter in, and will not be able.

When once the master of the house has risen up, and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside, and to knock at the door, saying: Lord, Lord, open to us. And he will answer and say to you: I do not know you, where you are from.
Then you will begin to say: We have eaten and drunk in your presence, and you have taught in our streets.
But he will say: I tell you, I do not know you, where you are from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity (sin).
There will be weeping and gnashing (grinding) of teeth, when you will see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.
And they will come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and will sit down in the kingdom of God.
And look, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.
The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying to Jesus: Get out, and depart from here, for Herod will kill You.
And Jesus said to them: Go, and tell that fox: Look, I cast out devils (demons), and I do cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I will be perfected (finished).
Nevertheless (even so) I must walk today, and tomorrow, and the day following. For it cannot be that a prophet perish (die) out of Jerusalem.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which kills the prophets, and stones them who are sent to you. How often would I have gathered your children together, as a hen gathers her brood (chicks) under her wings, and you would not.

Look, your house is left to you desolate (empty and ruined). And verily (truly) I say to you: You will not see Me, until the time comes when you will say: Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.

verses.text: And it came to pass (happened), as Jesus went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day (day of rest), that they watched Him.
And look, there was a certain man before Him who had the dropsy (a swelling sickness).
And Jesus answering spoke to the lawyers (experts in God's law) and Pharisees, saying: Is it lawful (allowed by the law) to heal on the sabbath day (day of rest)?
And they held their peace (were quiet). And Jesus took the man, and healed him, and let him go,
And answered them, saying: Which of you will have an ass (donkey) or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway (right away) pull him out on the sabbath day (day of rest)?
And they could not answer Him again to these things.
And Jesus put forth a parable (story that teaches a lesson) to those who were bidden (invited), when He marked (noticed) how they chose out the chief rooms (best seats), saying to them:
When you are bidden (invited) by any man to a wedding, do not sit down in the highest room (best seat), in case a more honourable man than you is bidden by him,
And he who bade (invited) you and him comes and says to you: Give this man place. And you begin with shame to take the lowest room (seat).

But when you are bidden (invited), go and sit down in the lowest room (seat), that when he who bade you comes, he may say to you: Friend, go up higher. Then you will have worship (honor) in the presence of them who sit at meat (the meal) with you.
For whoever exalts (lifts up) himself will be abased (brought low). And the one who humbles himself will be exalted (lifted up).

Then Jesus said also to him who bade (invited) Him: When you make a dinner or a supper, do not call your friends, nor your brothers, neither your kinsmen (relatives), nor your rich neighbours, in case they also bid (invite) you again, and a recompence (repayment) is made to you.
But when you make a feast, call the poor, the maimed (people with crippled bodies), the lame (people who cannot walk well), the blind,
And you will be blessed (happy). For they cannot recompense (repay) you. For you will be recompensed at the resurrection (rising from the dead) of the just (those who are right with God).
And when one of them who sat at meat (the meal) with Jesus heard these things, he said to Him: Blessed (happy) is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of God.
Then Jesus said to him: A certain man made a great supper, and bade (invited) many,
And sent his servant at supper time to say to them who were bidden (invited): Come, for all things are now ready.
And they all with one consent (together) began to make excuse. The first said to him: I have bought a piece of ground, and I must go and see it. I pray you have me excused.
And another said: I have bought 5 yoke (pairs) of oxen, and I go to prove (test) them. I pray you have me excused.
And another said: I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

So that servant came, and showed his lord (master) these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant: Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, and the maimed (people with crippled bodies), and the halt (crippled), and the blind.
And the servant said: Lord (master), it is done as you have commanded, and yet there is room.
And the lord (master) said to the servant: Go out into the highways (main roads) and hedges, and compel (urge) them to come in, that my house may be filled.
For I say to you, that none of those men who were bidden (invited) will taste of my supper.
And there went great multitudes (large crowds) with Jesus. And He turned, and said to them:
If anyone comes to Me, and does not hate their father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, yes, and their own life also, they cannot be My disciple.
And whoever does not bear (carry) their cross, and come after Me, cannot be My disciple.
For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not sit down first, and count the cost, whether they have enough to finish it?
Lest haply (in case), after they have laid the foundation, and are not able to finish it, all who behold (see) it begin to mock them,
Saying: This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
Or what king, going to make war against another king, does not sit down first, and consult (think) whether he is able with 10,000 to meet him who comes against him with 20,000?
Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an ambassage (group of messengers), and desires (asks for) conditions of peace.
So likewise, whoever of you does not forsake (leave) all that they have, they cannot be My disciple.
Salt is good. But if the salt has lost its savour (taste), with what will it be seasoned?
It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill (manure pile), but men cast it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
Then all the publicans (tax collectors) and sinners drew near to Jesus to hear Him.
And the Pharisees and scribes (teachers of the law) murmured (complained), saying: This man receives sinners, and eats with them.
And Jesus spoke this parable (story that teaches a lesson) to them, saying:
What man of you, having 100 sheep, if he loses one of them, does not leave the 99 in the wilderness (desert), and go after that which is lost, until he finds it?
And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbours, saying to them: Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost.
I say to you, that likewise joy will be in heaven over one sinner who repents (changes their heart), more than over 99 just (right with God) persons, who need no repentance (change of heart).
Or what woman having 10 pieces of silver, if she loses one piece, does not light a candle (lamp), and sweep the house, and seek diligently (search carefully) till she finds it?
And when she has found it, she calls her friends and her neighbours together, saying: Rejoice with me, for I have found the piece which I had lost.
Likewise, I say to you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents (changes their heart).
And Jesus said: A certain man had 2 sons.
And the younger of them said to his father: Father, give me the portion (share) of goods that falls to me. And the father divided to them his living (property).
And not many days after, the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance (money) with riotous (wild) living.
And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine (time of no food) in that land, and he began to be in want (need).
And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country. And the citizen sent him into his fields to feed swine (pigs).
And he would fain (gladly) have filled his belly (stomach) with the husks that the swine (pigs) ate. And no man gave to him.
And when he came to himself, he said: How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish (am dying) with hunger.
I will arise and go to my father, and will say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before you,
And am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.
And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion (deep pity), and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
And the son said to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight, and am no more worthy to be called your son.
But the father said to his servants: Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him. And put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.
And bring here the fatted calf (the calf made fat for a feast), and kill it. And let us eat, and be merry (happy).
For this my son was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry (happy).
Now his elder son was in the field. And as he came and drew nigh (near) to the house, he heard music and dancing.
And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
And the servant said to him: Your brother has come. And your father has killed the fatted calf, because he has received him safe and sound.
And the elder son was angry, and would not go in. Therefore his father came out, and intreated (begged) him.

And he answering said to his father: Look, these many years I serve you, neither did I transgress (break) at any time your commandment. And yet you never gave me a kid (young goat), that I might make merry (have a party) with my friends.
But as soon as this your son had come, who has devoured (wasted) your living with harlots (prostitutes), you have killed for him the fatted calf.
And the father said to him: Son, you are ever (always) with me, and all that I have is yours.
It was meet (right) that we should make merry (be happy), and be glad. For this your brother was dead, and is alive again, and was lost, and is found.

verses.text: And Jesus said also to His disciples: There was a certain rich man, who had a steward (manager). And the same was accused to him that he had wasted his goods.
And the rich man called him, and said to him: How is it that I hear this of you? Give an account of your stewardship (managing). For you may be no longer steward (manager).
Then the steward said within himself: What will I do? For my lord (master) takes away from me the stewardship (job of managing). I cannot dig. To beg I am ashamed.
I am resolved (have decided) what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship (job), they may receive me into their houses.
So he called every one of his lord's (master's) debtors (people who owed money) to him, and said to the first: How much do you owe to my lord?
And he said: 100 measures of oil. And the steward said to him: Take your bill, and sit down quickly, and write 50.
Then he said to another: And how much do you owe? And he said: 100 measures of wheat. And the steward said to him: Take your bill, and write 80.
And the lord (master) commended (praised) the unjust steward (manager), because he had done wisely. For the children of this world are in their generation (time) wiser than the children of light.
And I say to you: Make to yourselves friends of the mammon (money) of unrighteousness (wrong), that, when you fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations (homes).
The one who is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much. And the one who is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous (wrong) mammon (money), who will commit (trust) to you the true riches?
And if you have not been faithful in that which is another man's, who will give you that which is your own?
No servant can serve 2 masters. For either he will hate the one, and love the other. Or else he will hold to the one, and despise (look down on) the other. You cannot serve God and mammon (money).
And the Pharisees also, who were covetous (loved money), heard all these things. And they derided (made fun of) Jesus.

And Jesus said to them: You are they who justify (say you are right) yourselves before men. But God knows your hearts. For that which is highly esteemed (honored) among men is abomination (hateful) in the sight of God.
The law and the prophets were until John. Since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presses (pushes hard) into it.
And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass (go away), than one tittle (smallest mark) of the law to fail.
Whoever puts away (divorces) his wife, and marries another, commits adultery (being unfaithful in marriage). And whoever marries her who is put away (divorced) from her husband commits adultery.
There was a certain rich man, who was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously (lived richly) every day.
And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, who was laid at his gate, full of sores,
And desiring (wanting) to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table. Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
And it came to pass (happened), that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom (side). The rich man also died, and was buried.
And in hell he lifted up his eyes, being in torments (great pain), and sees Abraham far off, and Lazarus in his bosom (at his side).
And he cried and said: Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue. For I am tormented (in great pain) in this flame.
But Abraham said: Son, remember that you in your lifetime received your good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things. But now he is comforted, and you are tormented (in great pain).
And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf (deep gap) fixed, so that they who would pass from here to you cannot. Neither can they pass to us, who would come from there.
Then he said: I pray you therefore, father, that you would send Lazarus to my father's house,
For I have 5 brothers, that he may testify (warn) to them, so that they will not also come into this place of torment (great pain).
Abraham says to him: They have Moses and the prophets. Let them hear them.
And he said: No, father Abraham. But if one went to them from the dead, they will repent (change their hearts).
And Abraham said to him: If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

verses.text: Then Jesus said to the disciples: It is impossible but that offences (things that cause sin) will come. But woe (great trouble) to the one through whom they come.
It would be better for them that a millstone (large heavy stone) were hanged about their neck, and they were cast into the sea, than that they should offend (cause to sin) one of these little ones.
Take heed (be careful) to yourselves. If your brother trespass (does wrong) against you, rebuke (correct) him. And if he repent (changes his heart), forgive him.
And if he trespass (does wrong) against you 7 times in a day, and 7 times in a day turns again to you, saying: I repent (I am sorry), you will forgive him.
And the apostles (sent ones) said to the Lord: Increase our faith.
And the Lord said: If you had faith as a grain of mustard seed, you might say to this sycamine (mulberry) tree: Be plucked up by the root, and be planted in the sea. And it would obey you.
But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say to him by and by (right away), when he has come from the field: Go and sit down to meat (eat a meal)?
And will not rather say to him: Make ready that I may sup (eat supper), and gird (dress) yourself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunk. And afterward you will eat and drink?
Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow (think) not.
So likewise you, when you will have done all those things which are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable (useless) servants. We have done that which was our duty to do.
And it came to pass (happened), as Jesus went to Jerusalem, that He passed through the middle of Samaria and Galilee.
And as Jesus entered into a certain village, there met Him 10 men who were lepers (people with a skin disease), who stood afar off (far away).
And they lifted up their voices, and said: Jesus, Master (Teacher), have mercy on us.
And when Jesus saw them, He said to them: Go show yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass (happened), that, as they went, they were cleansed (healed).
And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified (praised) God,
And fell down on his face at Jesus' feet, giving Him thanks. And he was a Samaritan.
And Jesus answering said: Were there not 10 cleansed (healed)? But where are the 9?
There are not found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger.
And Jesus said to him: Arise (get up), go your way. Your faith has made you whole (healed you).
And when Jesus was demanded (asked) by the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God would come, He answered them and said: The kingdom of God does not come with observation (outward signs to watch).
Neither will they say: Look here, or, look there. For look, the kingdom of God is within you.
And Jesus said to the disciples: The days will come, when you will desire (want) to see one of the days of the Son of man, and you will not see it.
And they will say to you: See here, or, see there. Do not go after them, nor follow them.
For as the lightning, that lightens out of the one part under heaven, shines to the other part under heaven, so will also the Son of man be in His day.
But first He must suffer many things, and be rejected by this generation (people living now).
And as it was in the days of Noe (Noah), so will it be also in the days of the Son of man.
They ate, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe (Noah) entered into the ark (big boat), and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built.
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone (burning sulfur) from heaven, and destroyed them all.
Even so will it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed (shown).
In that day, whoever will be upon the housetop, and their stuff (goods) in the house, let them not come down to take it away. And whoever is in the field, let them likewise not return back.
Remember Lot's wife.
Whoever will seek to save their life will lose it. And whoever will lose their life will preserve (keep) it.
I tell you, in that night there will be 2 men in one bed. The one will be taken, and the other will be left.
There will be 2 women grinding (grain) together. The one will be taken, and the other left.
There will be 2 men in the field. The one will be taken, and the other left.
And they answered and said to Jesus: Where, Lord? And He said to them: Wherever the body is, there will the eagles be gathered together.

Covers the parable of the persistent widow and the unjust judge, the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector, blessing the little children, the rich ruler, the third prediction of Jesus' death, and healing a blind beggar near Jericho.

verses.text: Then Jesus told His disciples a teaching story to show them that they should always pray and not give up.
He said: In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor cared what people thought.
And there was a widow in that town who kept coming to him with the plea: Grant me justice against my adversary.
For some time he refused. But finally he said to himself: Even though I do not fear God or care what people think,
Yet because this widow keeps bothering me, I will see that she gets justice, so that she will not eventually wear me out with her coming.
And the Lord said: Listen to what the unjust judge says.
And will not God bring about justice for His chosen ones, who cry out to Him day and night? Will He keep putting them off?
I tell you, He will see that they get justice, and quickly. However, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on the earth?
To some who were confident of their own righteousness and looked down on everyone else, Jesus told this teaching story:
Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed: God, I thank you that I am not like other people: robbers, evildoers, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week and give a tenth of all I get.
But the tax collector stood at a distance. He would not even look up to heaven, but beat his breast and said: God, have mercy on me, a sinner.
I tell you that this man, rather than the other, went home justified before God. For all those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.
People were also bringing babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. When the disciples saw this, they rebuked them.
But Jesus called the children to Him. He said: Let the little children come to me. Do not hinder them. The kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I tell you, anyone who will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.
A certain ruler asked Him: Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?
Why do you call me good? Jesus answered. No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Honor your father and mother.
All these I have kept since I was a boy, he said.
When Jesus heard this, He said to him: You still lack one thing. Sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.
When he heard this, he became very sad, because he was very wealthy.
Jesus looked at him and said: How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!
Indeed, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.
Those who heard this asked: Who then can be saved?
Jesus replied: What is impossible with man is possible with God.
Peter said to Him: We have left all we had to follow You!
Jesus said to them: I tell you the truth. Suppose someone has left home, wife, brothers, sisters, parents, or children. That person did it for the sake of the kingdom of God.
That person will certainly receive many times as much in this present time. And in the coming age, that person will receive eternal life.
Jesus took the Twelve aside and told them: We are going up to Jerusalem. Everything that is written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
He will be delivered over to the Gentiles. They will mock Him, insult Him, spit on Him,
And flog Him and kill Him. On the third day He will rise again.
The disciples did not understand any of this. Its meaning was hidden from them, and they did not know what he was talking about.
As Jesus approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the road begging.
When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
They told him: Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.
He called out: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!
Those who led the way rebuked him and told him to be quiet, but he shouted all the more: Son of David, have mercy on me!
Jesus stopped and ordered the man to be brought to Him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
What do you want me to do for you? Lord, he said, I want to see.
Jesus said to him: Receive your sight; your faith has healed you.
Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, praising God. When all the people saw it, they also praised God.

verses.text: Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.
A man was there named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector and was wealthy.
He wanted to see who Jesus was, but he was too short and could not see over the crowd.
So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree to see Him, since Jesus was coming that way.
When Jesus reached the spot, He looked up and said to him: Zacchaeus, come down immediately. I must stay at your house today.
So he came down at once and welcomed Him gladly.
All the people saw this and began to mutter: He has gone to be the guest of a sinner.
But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord: Look, Lord! Here and now I give half of my possessions to the poor. If I have cheated anyone, I will pay back four times as much.
Jesus said to him: Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.
While they were listening to this, He went on to tell them a teaching story. He was near Jerusalem, and the people thought the kingdom of God was going to appear at once.
He said: A man of noble birth went to a distant country to have himself appointed king and then to return.
So he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. Put this money to work, he said, until I come back.
But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say: We do not want this man to be our king.
He was made king, however, and returned home. Then he sent for the servants to whom he had given the money, in order to find out what they had gained with it.
The first one came and said: Sir, your mina has earned ten more.
Well done, my good servant! his master replied. Because you have been trustworthy in a very small matter, take charge of ten cities.
The second came and said: Sir, your mina has earned five more.
His master answered: You take charge of five cities.
Then another servant came and said: Sir, here is your mina. I have kept it laid away in a piece of cloth.
I was afraid of you, because you are a hard man. You take out what you did not put in, and reap what you did not sow.
His master replied: I will judge you by your own words, you wicked servant! You knew, did you, that I am a hard man, taking out what I did not put in, and reaping what I did not sow?
Why then did you not put my money on deposit, so that when I came back I could have collected it with interest?
Then he said to those standing by: Take his mina away from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.
Sir, they said, he already has ten!
He replied: I tell you, everyone who has will be given more, but the one who has nothing will have even what they have taken away.
But those enemies of mine who did not want me to be king over them, bring them here and kill them in front of me.
After Jesus had said this, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
As He approached Bethphage and Bethany at the hill called the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples, saying:
Go to the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, which no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks you: Why are you untying it? say: The Lord needs it.
Those who were sent ahead went and found it just as He had told them.
As they were untying the colt, its owners asked them: Why are you untying the colt?
They replied: The Lord needs it.
They brought it to Jesus, threw their cloaks on the colt, and put Jesus on it.
As He went along, people spread their cloaks on the road.

When He came near the place where the road goes down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of disciples began to praise God. They praised Him joyfully in loud voices for all the miracles they had seen:
Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!
Some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus: Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!
I tell you, He replied, if they keep quiet, the stones will cry out.
As He approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it
And said: If you, even you, had only known on this day what would bring you peace. But now it is hidden from your eyes.
The days will come upon you when your enemies will build an embankment against you and encircle you and hem you in on every side.
They will dash you to the ground, you and the children within your walls. They will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognize the time of God's coming to you.
When Jesus entered the temple courts, He began to drive out those who were selling.
It is written, He said to them, My house will be a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of robbers.
Every day He was teaching at the temple. But the chief priests, the teachers of the law, and the leaders among the people were trying to kill Him.
Yet they could not find any way to do it, because all the people hung on His words.
One day Jesus was in the temple teaching people. Jesus told them the Good News. The chief priests and the teachers of the law came to talk to Jesus
And asked Him: Tell us what authority You have to do these things. Who gave You this authority?
Jesus said to them: I will ask you one question.
John the Baptist came, and he baptized people. Who sent John to do it? Was it God who sent John, or did the people send John?
They talked to each other and said: Suppose we say that John was sent by God. Jesus will ask us: Why did you not believe what John said?
But if we say that John's baptism was from someone else, the people will stone us to death. They all believe that John was a prophet.
So they answered: We do not know who sent John.
Then Jesus said to them: Then I will not tell you who told me that I may do these things.
Jesus told the people this story. He said: A man planted a vineyard. Then he rented out the vineyard to other farmers and went on a journey for a long time to another country.

When it was time to pick the grapes, the owner sent a servant to the farmers who rented his vineyard. The owner asked the farmers to give the servant his share of the grapes. The farmers grabbed the servant and beat him and chased him away. The farmers gave the servant no grapes.
The owner sent another servant to the farmers. They took this servant and beat him also. They dishonored him, and they gave him no grapes.
The owner then sent a third servant, but the farmers beat him too, and they threw him out of the vineyard.
Then the owner said: What can I do? I will send my son, whom I love very much. I think they will respect my son.
But when the farmers saw the son, they said to each other: This son will inherit everything one day. Let us kill him, so that we will get it all.
So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What do you think the owner will do to those farmers? Jesus asked.
He will come and kill those farmers and give the vineyard to others. When the people heard this, they said: This must never happen.

But Jesus looked into their eyes and said: If you say that this must never happen, what do these words in the book of Psalms mean? The stone that the builders did not want to use is now the most important stone in the building.
Everyone who falls over this stone will die and break his legs. And if this stone falls on anyone, it will scatter him like dust.
The teachers of the law and the chief priests looked for a way to arrest Jesus immediately. They knew He had told this teaching story against them. But they were afraid of the people.

Keeping a close watch on Him, they sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They hoped to catch Jesus in something He said, so that they could hand Him over to the power and authority of the Roman governor.
The spies then asked Jesus: Teacher, we know that what You say and teach is true. It does not matter who is listening, You teach the same to all people. You always teach the truth about God's way.
Now tell us: Is it right to pay taxes to Caesar? Must we pay taxes to him or not?
But Jesus knew that these men were trying to trick Him. Jesus said to them: Why are you trying to test me?
Show me a coin, Jesus said. Whose head and whose name is on this money? They answered him: It is Caesar's head and his name.
Jesus said to the spies: That is right. Then you must give to Caesar what belongs to him, but you must also give to God what belongs to Him.
The men were amazed at His wise answer. They could say nothing. They were not able to trick Jesus there in front of the people. He said nothing they could use against Him.
Some of the Sadducees, who believe that people will not rise from death, came to Jesus and said:
Teacher, Moses wrote that if a married man dies and has no children, his brother must marry his widow. Then they will have children for the dead brother.
Now, there were seven brothers. The oldest brother married a woman, but he died, and they did not have any children.
The 2nd brother then married the widow of the oldest brother, but he also died, and they did not have any children.
The same happened with the third brother. He also married her, and he died. It happened to all seven brothers. All of them married this woman but they did not have any children.
Later, the woman also died.
Now we ask You, Jesus: Whose wife will this woman be when all the dead people rise and live again? Because all of these seven brothers were married to her.
Jesus said to the Sadducees: In this life people get married.
But when God is King, He will give life to all the people who have believed in Jesus and have died. Then people will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
They will be like the angels in heaven who do not die and who live with God in heaven. They will be children of God because God gave them life and made them live again.

Moses also said that people who have died will rise and live again. He wrote about it when he spoke about the burning bush. There God said to Moses: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
God is not the God of dead people. He is the God of people who live.
Some of the teachers of the law responded: Well said, teacher!
From that day on the people were afraid to ask Jesus any more questions.
Then Jesus said to them: Why is it said that the Messiah is the son of David?
David says in the book of Psalms: The Lord God said to my Lord: Sit by me at my right side,
I will make your enemies bow before you. You will put your feet on them.
David calls Him Lord. How then can He be His son?
While all the people were listening, Jesus said to his disciples,

Watch out for the teachers of the law. They like to walk around in flowing robes. They love to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces. They love the most important seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.
They devour widows' houses and for a show make lengthy prayers. Such people will be punished most severely.

20.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Fixed two merged-verse numbering bugs (5/6, 31/32), a stray text fragment, and several grammar issues.

21.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter was previously missing from the site entirely. Covers the widow's offering (praised for giving out of her poverty), and Jesus' Olivet Discourse: the prediction of the temple's destruction, signs of persecution and the end times, and the coming of the Son of Man.

verses.text: As Jesus looked up, He saw the rich putting their gifts into the temple treasury.
He also saw a poor widow put in two very small copper coins.
Truly I tell you, He said, this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
All these people gave their gifts out of their wealth, but she out of her poverty put in all she had to live on.
Some of His disciples were remarking about how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and with gifts dedicated to God. But Jesus said,
As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another. Every one of them will be thrown down.
Teacher, they asked, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?
He replied: Watch out that you are not deceived. For many will come in my name, claiming: I am He, and: The time is near. Do not follow them.
When you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be frightened. These things must happen first, but the end will not come right away.
Then He said to them: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in various places, and fearful events and great signs from heaven.
But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you. They will hand you over to synagogues and put you in prison. You will be brought before kings and governors on account of my name.
And so you will bear testimony to me.
But make up your mind not to worry beforehand how you will defend yourselves.
For I will give you words and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.
You will be betrayed even by parents, brothers and sisters, relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
Everyone will hate you because of me.
But not a hair of your head will perish.
Stand firm, and you will win life.
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that its desolation is near.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Let those in the city get out. Let those in the country not enter the city.
For this is the time of punishment in fulfillment of all that has been written.
How dreadful it will be in those days for pregnant women and nursing mothers! There will be great distress in the land and wrath against this people.
They will fall by the sword and will be taken as prisoners to all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled on by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
There will be signs in the sun, moon, and stars. On the earth, nations will be in anguish and perplexity at the roaring and tossing of the sea.
People will faint from terror, apprehensive of what is coming on the world, for the heavenly bodies will be shaken.
At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
When these things begin to take place, stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.
Jesus told them this teaching story: Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.
Even so, when you see these things happening, you know that the kingdom of God is near.
Truly I tell you, this generation will certainly not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
Be careful, or your hearts will be weighed down with wild parties, drunkenness, and the worries of life. That day will close on you suddenly like a trap.
For it will come on all those who live on the face of the whole earth.
Always be on the watch. Pray that you will be able to escape all that is about to happen. Pray that you will be able to stand before the Son of Man.
Each day Jesus was teaching at the temple, and each evening He went out to spend the night on the hill called the Mount of Olives,
And all the people came early in the morning to hear Him at the temple.

22.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter was previously missing from the site entirely. Covers Judas' betrayal deal, the Last Supper and the dispute over who is greatest, Jesus' prediction of Peter's denial, Gethsemane (including the angel and the sweat like drops of blood), the arrest and healing of the servant's ear, Peter's three denials, and the trial before the Sanhedrin.

verses.text: Now the Festival of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, was approaching,
And the chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for some way to get rid of Jesus, for they were afraid of the people.
Then Satan entered Judas, called Iscariot, one of the Twelve.
Judas went to the chief priests and the officers of the temple guard and discussed with them how he might betray Jesus.
They were delighted and agreed to give him money.
He consented, and watched for an opportunity to hand Jesus over to them when no crowd was present.
Then came the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying: Go and make preparations for us to eat the Passover.
Where do you want us to prepare for it? they asked.
He replied: As you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him to the house that he enters,
And say to the owner of the house: The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?
He will show you a large room upstairs, all furnished. Make preparations there.
They went and found things just as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When the hour came, Jesus and His apostles reclined at the table.
And He said to them: I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it finds fulfillment in the kingdom of God.
After taking the cup, He gave thanks and said: Take this and divide it among you.
For I tell you, I will not drink again from the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.
And He took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying: This is my body given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.
In the same way, after the supper He took the cup, saying: This cup is the new agreement in my blood, which is poured out for you.
But the hand of him who is going to betray me is with mine on the table.
The Son of Man will go as it has been decreed, but woe to that man who betrays him.
They began to question among themselves which of them it might be who would do this.
A dispute also arose among them as to which of them was considered to be greatest.
Jesus said to them: The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them call themselves benefactors.
But you are not to be like that. Instead, the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who rules like the one who serves.
For who is greater, the one who is at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who is at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
You are those who have stood by me in my trials.
And I confer on you a kingdom, just as my Father conferred one on me,
So that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift all of you as wheat.
But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith may not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.
But he replied: Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death.
Jesus answered: I tell you, Peter, before the rooster crows today, you will deny three times that you know me.
Then Jesus asked them: When I sent you without purse, bag, or sandals, did you lack anything? Nothing, they answered.
He said to them: But now, if you have a purse, take it, and also a bag. And if you do not have a sword, sell your cloak and buy one.
It is written: He was numbered with the transgressors. I tell you that this must be fulfilled in me. Yes, what is written about me is reaching its fulfillment.
The disciples said: See, Lord, here are two swords. That is enough, He replied.
Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives, and His disciples followed Him.
On reaching the place, He said to them: Pray that you will not fall into temptation.
He withdrew about a stone's throw beyond them, knelt down and prayed,
Father, if you are willing, take this cup from me. Yet not my will, but yours be done.
An angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him.
And being in anguish, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat was like drops of blood falling to the ground.
When He rose from prayer and went back to the disciples, He found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow.
Why are you sleeping? He asked them. Get up and pray so that you will not fall into temptation.
While He was still speaking, a crowd came, and the man who was called Judas, one of the Twelve, was leading them. He approached Jesus to kiss Him,
But Jesus asked him: Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?
When Jesus' followers saw what was going to happen, they said: Lord, should we strike with our swords?
And one of them struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear.
But Jesus answered: No more of this! And He touched the man's ear and healed him.
Jesus spoke to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders coming for Him. He asked: Am I leading a rebellion? Is that why you have come with swords and clubs?
Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on me. But this is your hour, when darkness reigns.
Then seizing Him, they led Him away and took Him into the house of the high priest. Peter followed at a distance.
And when some there had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and had sat down together, Peter sat down with them.
A servant girl saw him seated there in the firelight. She looked closely at him and said: This man was with him.
But he denied it: Woman, I do not know him.
A little later someone else saw him and said: You also are one of them. Man, I am not! Peter replied.
About an hour later another asserted: Certainly this fellow was with him, for he is a Galilean.
Peter replied: Man, I do not know what you are talking about! Just as he was speaking, the rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked straight at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word the Lord had spoken to him: Before the rooster crows today, you will disown me three times.
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
The men who were guarding Jesus began mocking and beating Him.
They blindfolded Him and demanded: Prophesy! Who hit You?
And they said many other insulting things to Him.
At daybreak the council of the elders of the people met together. It included both the chief priests and the teachers of the law. Then Jesus was led before them.
If you are the Messiah, tell us, they said. Jesus answered: If I tell you, you will not believe me,
And if I asked you, you would not answer.
But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the mighty God.
They all asked: Are you then the Son of God? He replied: You say that I am.
Then they said: Why do we need any more testimony? We have heard it ourselves from His own lips.

23.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter was previously missing from the site entirely -- its completion finishes the whole Gospel of Luke. Covers the trial before Pilate and Herod, the crowd choosing Barabbas, the crucifixion (including the penitent thief's exchange with Jesus, found only in Luke), Jesus' death, and his burial by Joseph of Arimathea.

verses.text: Then the whole assembly rose and led Him off to Pilate.
And they began to accuse Him, saying: We have found this man subverting our nation. He opposes payment of taxes to Caesar and claims to be Messiah, a king.
So Pilate asked Jesus: Are you the king of the Jews? You have said so, Jesus replied.
Then Pilate announced to the chief priests and the crowd: I find no basis for a charge against this man.
But they insisted: He stirs up the people all over Judea by His teaching. He started in Galilee and has come all the way here.
On hearing this, Pilate asked if the man was a Galilean.
When he learned that Jesus was under Herod's jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem at that time.
When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased, because for a long time he had been wanting to see Him. From what he had heard about Him, he hoped to see Him perform a sign of some sort.
He plied Him with many questions, but Jesus gave him no answer.
The chief priests and the teachers of the law were standing there, vehemently accusing Him.
Then Herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked Him. Dressing Him in an elegant robe, they sent Him back to Pilate.
That day Herod and Pilate became friends. Before this they had been enemies.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,
And said to them: You brought me this man as one who was inciting the people to rebellion. I have examined Him in your presence and have found no basis for your charges against Him.
Neither has Herod, for he sent Him back to us. As you can see, He has done nothing to deserve death.
Therefore I will punish Him and then release Him.
For it was necessary for him to release one prisoner to them at the festival.
But the whole crowd shouted: Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!
(Barabbas had been thrown into prison for an insurrection in the city, and for murder.)
Wanting to release Jesus, Pilate appealed to them again.
But they kept shouting: Crucify Him! Crucify Him!
For the third time he spoke to them: Why? What crime has this man committed? I have found in Him no grounds for the death penalty. Therefore I will have Him punished and then release Him.
But with loud shouts they insistently demanded that He be crucified, and their shouts prevailed.
So Pilate decided to grant their demand.
He released the man who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, the one they asked for, and surrendered Jesus to their will.
As they led Him away, they seized Simon from Cyrene. He was on his way in from the country. They put the cross on him. They made him carry it behind Jesus.
A large number of people followed Him, including women who mourned and wailed for Him.
Jesus turned and said to them: Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
For the time will come when you will say: Blessed are the childless women, the wombs that never bore and the breasts that never nursed.
Then they will say to the mountains: Fall on us! and to the hills: Cover us!
For if people do these things when the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?
Two other men, both criminals, were also led out with Him to be executed.
When they came to the place called the Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right, the other on His left.
Jesus said: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing. And they divided up His clothes by casting lots.
The people stood watching, and the rulers even sneered at Him. They said: He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is God's Messiah, the Chosen One.
The soldiers also came up and mocked Him. They offered Him wine vinegar
And said: If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself.
There was a written notice above Him, which read: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
One of the criminals who hung there hurled insults at Him: Are you not the Messiah? Save yourself and us!
But the other criminal rebuked Him: Do you not fear God, since you are under the same sentence?
We are punished justly, for we are getting what our deeds deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.
Then he said: Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.
Jesus answered him: Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.
It was now about noon, and darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon,
For the sun stopped shining. And the curtain of the temple was torn in two.
Jesus called out with a loud voice: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit. When He had said this, He breathed His last.
The centurion, seeing what had happened, praised God and said: Surely this was a righteous man.
When all the people who had gathered to witness this sight saw what took place, they beat their breasts and went away.
But all those who knew Him, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, stood at a distance, watching these things.
Now there was a man named Joseph, a member of the Council, a good and upright man,
Who had not consented to their decision and action. He came from the Judean town of Arimathea, and he himself was waiting for the kingdom of God.
Going to Pilate, he asked for Jesus' body.
Then he took it down and wrapped it in linen cloth. He placed it in a tomb cut in the rock. No one had yet been laid in that tomb.
It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was about to begin.
The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed and saw the tomb and how His body was laid in it.
Then they went home and prepared spices and perfumes. But they rested on the Sabbath in obedience to the commandment.
Very early Sunday morning, the women came to the tomb where Jesus' body was laid. They brought the sweet-smelling spices they had prepared.
When the women came to the tomb, they saw that someone had rolled away the stone that was in front of the tomb.
The women went into the tomb but they did not see the body of the Lord Jesus there.
The women did not understand what had happened. While they were thinking about this, two men in shining clothes stood beside them.
The women were afraid and they bowed down with their faces to the ground. The men said to them: Why do you look for the One who lives, here in a tomb for dead people?
Jesus is not here. God has raised Him up and made Him live again. Remember what Jesus told you when you were in Galilee.
Jesus said God would give Him to bad people and they would kill Him, the Son of Man. They would nail Jesus to the cross but on the third day Jesus would rise and live again.
The women then remembered what Jesus had said.
The women went back home and told everything to the eleven apostles and the other believers.
The women who saw what happened at the tomb were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and some other women with them. When they told these things to the apostles,
The apostles did not believe them. They said it could not be true.

Then Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Peter bowed down and looked into the tomb and he saw only the cloth that they had put around the body of Jesus. Peter went back and was very surprised about what had happened.
That same Sunday, two of the men who followed Jesus walked to the town of Emmaus. It is about seven miles from Jerusalem.
They talked to each other about everything that had happened to Jesus.
While they were talking and thinking about the events that had happened, Jesus came and walked with them.
But they did not know that it was Jesus. Jesus did not want them to know at that time who He was.
Jesus asked them: Why are you so sad? What are you talking about as you walk down this road?
Cleopas, one of the men, asked Jesus: You must be the only person in Jerusalem who does not know what has just happened there.

Jesus asked them: What things? They said: All the things that happened to Jesus, the Man from Nazareth. Jesus was a prophet who did wonderful miracles. Jesus was a Teacher from God. God was with Him and all the people listened to Jesus.
But the chief leading priests and our leaders handed Him over to be judged and killed. They nailed Him to a cross.
We were hoping that Jesus would be the one to free Israel. But then all this happened. And it has been three days since Jesus was killed.
Also, today some of our women told us an amazing thing. Early this morning they went to the tomb where the body of Jesus was laid.
But the women did not find Jesus' body there. They came and told us they had seen some angels in a vision. The angels told them Jesus was alive!
So some of our group went to the tomb too. It was just as the women said. They saw the tomb, but they did not see Jesus.
Jesus said to them: You are foolish and slow to realize what is true. You should believe everything the prophets said.
The prophets said the Messiah must suffer these things before He begins His time of glory.
Then Jesus started to explain to them what the books of Moses and the prophets and the other books of the Old Testament said about Jesus.
When they got near the town of Emmaus, Jesus said He wanted to go to the next town.
But they wanted Jesus to stay. They begged Jesus: Stay with us. It is almost night. There is hardly any daylight left. So Jesus went in to stay with them.
When they started to eat, Jesus took the bread and thanked God for it. Jesus broke the bread and gave it to them.
Immediately God opened their eyes and they saw that it was Jesus. But then Jesus disappeared. They could not see Jesus anymore.
They said to each other: Now we know why we were so happy when Jesus talked to us on the road. When Jesus explained the Bible to us.
They immediately got up and went back to Jerusalem. They found the eleven apostles and other believers with them.
They said: The Lord really has risen from death! Jesus did appear to Simon.
Then they told the apostles and other people everything that had happened on the road to Emmaus. They told how they saw that it was Jesus when He broke the bread.
While the two men were saying these things to the other followers, Jesus stood there with them and Jesus said to them: Peace be with you.
The followers of Jesus were afraid. They thought they had seen a ghost.
But Jesus said to them: Why are you afraid? Why do you not believe what you see?
Look at my hands and my feet. It is really me. Touch me. You can see that I have a living body; ghost does not have a body with flesh and bones.
After Jesus said this, Jesus showed His followers His hands and His feet.
His followers were amazed and very, very happy to see that Jesus was alive. But they still could not believe what they saw. Jesus said to them: Do you have any food here?
They gave Jesus a piece of fish and honey.
Jesus took it and His followers watched Jesus eat it.

Then Jesus said to His followers: Do you remember what I said when I was with you before I died? I told you that everything written about me must happen. This includes the books of Moses, the books of the prophets, and the book of Psalms.
Then Jesus helped them to understand the Bible.
Jesus told His followers: The Old Testament says that the Christ must suffer and die. It also says that the Christ will rise and start to live again on the third day.

It is written that people who believe in God must go and tell everyone this: God forgives the sins of everyone who believes in Christ. God forgives everyone who turns to Him and starts living as He wants. You must start telling this to the people in Jerusalem.
Tell the people what you saw me do and what I said.
And I will send upon you what my Father has promised. But you must wait in the city of Jerusalem, until the power from above comes down upon you.
Then Jesus told the apostles to go with Him. Jesus took the apostles to a place near the town of Bethany. Then Jesus held up His hands and blessed them.
Jesus blessed the apostles then He was separated from them and carried into heaven.
The apostles worshipped Jesus and then they went back to Jerusalem. They were very happy.
They went to the temple every day and they praised God.
